learn.rule: A paragraph has one topic sentence and detail sentences. Every detail tells more about the big idea.
learn.ruleEs: Un párrafo tiene una oración temática y oraciones de detalle. Cada detalle dice más sobre la idea principal.
learn.model: Ladybugs are helpful garden insects. They eat tiny bugs that hurt plants. This keeps the garden healthy.
learn.notice: Look at the first sentence. It tells the big idea. The other sentences are details about ladybugs.

items.prompt: Read the three details about hive bees. Which topic sentence fits all of them?
items.text: Worker bees gather nectar. Some bees guard the door of the hive. Other bees feed the baby bees.

options.text: Bees collect nectar.
Every bee in a hive has a job to do.
Honey tastes sweet on warm toast.

items.why: A topic sentence tells the big idea for the whole paragraph. This one covers gathering, guarding, and feeding. The other choices are too small or about something else.
items.whyEs: Una oración temática dice la idea principal de todo el párrafo. Esta cubre recolectar, cuidar y alimentar. Las otras opciones son muy pequeñas o hablan de otra cosa.

items.prompt: Which sentence does not belong in the bee paragraph?
items.text: Bees live together in a hive. A hive can hold thousands of bees. Our bus driver drives very carefully. The bees keep the hive warm in winter.

options.text: The bees keep the hive warm in winter.
Our bus driver drives very carefully.
A hive can hold thousands of bees.

items.why: Every detail must be about the big idea. The bus driver sentence is about a different topic, so it does not belong.
items.whyEs: Cada detalle debe tratar de la idea principal. La oración del conductor del autobús trata de otro tema, así que no pertenece.

items.prompt: Check every detail that belongs with this topic sentence: 'Bees are helpful garden visitors.'

options.text: They carry pollen from flower to flower.
Penguins live where it is very cold.
Pollen helps plants make seeds and fruit.
My bike has a red seat.

items.why: Good details give more information about the topic sentence. Moving pollen and helping plants make fruit are both about helpful bees.
items.whyEs: Los buenos detalles dan más información sobre la oración temática. Llevar polen y ayudar a las plantas a dar fruto tratan de abejas útiles.

items.prompt: Pick the signal word that adds an example detail.
parts: , they help pumpkin flowers grow into pumpkins.
items.model: Bees are helpful garden visitors. For example, they help pumpkin flowers grow into pumpkins.
items.why: For example tells the reader that a detail is coming. It connects the detail to the topic sentence.
items.whyEs: For example avisa al lector que viene un detalle. Une el detalle con la oración temática.

items.prompt: Put the sentences of this paragraph about how a bee grows in order.
lines: A bee grows and changes in steps.
First, the queen lays an egg in a small cell.
Next, the egg hatches into a larva that workers feed.
Last, the larva rests in its cell and changes into an adult bee.
items.why: The topic sentence comes first. Then the signal words first, next, and last put the details in order.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero. Luego las palabras first, next y last ponen los detalles en orden.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best closing sentence for this paragraph about a hive?
items.text: A hive is a busy bee home. Workers gather nectar and clean the cells. The queen lays the eggs.

options.text: Bees also make wax for the hive.
I like honey on warm toast.
Together, the bees keep their hive working well.

items.why: A closing sentence wraps up the big idea. It does not add a new detail and it does not wander to a new topic.
items.whyEs: Una oración final cierra la idea principal. No agrega un detalle nuevo ni se va a otro tema.

write.prompt: Write a paragraph about ants. Start with a topic sentence, then add two detail sentences.
write.promptEs: Escribe un párrafo sobre las hormigas. Empieza con una oración temática y luego agrega dos oraciones de detalle.
write.text: Big idea: ants are strong and hard-working.

label: I wrote a topic sentence and two details
Escribí una oración temática y dos detalles

write.model: Ants are strong, hard-working insects. An ant can carry food much heavier than its own body. Ants also dig tunnels to build a home underground.

familyTalk.en: At dinner, one person says a big idea, like 'Our pet is funny.' Everyone adds one detail.
familyTalk.es: En la cena, una persona dice una idea principal, como 'Nuestra mascota es divertida'. Todos agregan un detalle.

teacherTip.en: Read each paragraph aloud and ask students to point to the topic sentence before they choose.
teacherTip.es: Lee cada párrafo en voz alta y pide que señalen la oración temática antes de elegir.

learn.rule: A topic sentence tells the big idea. Detail sentences give facts, examples, or reasons about it.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración temática dice la idea principal. Las oraciones de detalle dan datos, ejemplos o razones sobre ella.
learn.model: Crossing guards keep students safe. They stop cars so children can cross the street. They also wave and say good morning.
learn.notice: The first sentence names the big idea. Each detail tells how crossing guards help.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence fits all three details about letter carriers?
items.text: Letter carriers deliver mail to our homes. They also bring packages to our doors. They walk or drive their routes every day.

options.text: Stamps come in many colors.
Letter carriers do an important job for our town.
Letter carriers bring packages.

items.why: The best topic sentence is big enough to cover all the details. Packages are only one detail, and stamps are a different topic.
items.whyEs: La mejor oración temática es lo bastante grande para cubrir todos los detalles. Los paquetes son solo un detalle y los sellos son otro tema.

items.prompt: Which sentence does not belong in the paragraph about school helpers?
items.text: Helpers at our school make learning easier. The librarian helps us find books. Pizza is my favorite lunch. The nurse helps us feel better.

options.text: The librarian helps us find books.
The nurse helps us feel better.
Pizza is my favorite lunch.

items.why: A detail has to be about the big idea. Pizza is about lunch, not about school helpers.
items.whyEs: Un detalle debe tratar de la idea principal. La pizza trata del almuerzo, no de los ayudantes de la escuela.

items.prompt: Check every detail that belongs with this topic sentence: 'Firefighters keep our town safe.'

options.text: They put out fires in homes and buildings.
Teachers help students learn to read.
They visit schools to teach fire safety.
Farmers grow food for many families.
They rescue people who are in danger.

items.why: Each detail that belongs shows one way firefighters keep people safe. The teachers and farmers are helpers too, but they are a different topic.
items.whyEs: Cada detalle correcto muestra una forma en que los bomberos mantienen seguras a las personas. Los maestros y los agricultores también ayudan, pero son otro tema.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that starts an added detail.
parts: , they visit schools to teach fire safety.
items.model: Firefighters keep our town safe. In addition, they visit schools to teach fire safety.
items.why: In addition tells the reader that one more detail is coming. The other choices change the time or the meaning.
items.whyEs: In addition avisa que viene un detalle más. Las otras opciones cambian el tiempo o el significado.

items.prompt: Put the sentences about how a letter travels in order.
lines: Mail travels a long way to reach your home.
First, a person drops a letter in a mailbox.
Next, a truck takes the letter to a sorting center.
Last, a letter carrier brings it to the right house.
items.why: The topic sentence goes first, then first, next, and last show the steps in order.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero. Luego first, next y last muestran los pasos en orden.

items.prompt: Which closing sentence best finishes the firefighter paragraph?
items.text: Firefighters keep our town safe. They put out fires. They visit schools to teach fire safety.

options.text: Fire trucks are very loud.
Police officers wear badges.
Firefighters are important helpers in our town.

items.why: A closing sentence says the big idea again in new words. It does not bring in a new detail or a new topic.
items.whyEs: Una oración final repite la idea principal con otras palabras. No trae un detalle ni un tema nuevo.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two details about a helper at our school, such as a custodian or a cook.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos detalles sobre un ayudante de nuestra escuela, como el conserje o el cocinero.

label: I wrote a topic sentence and two details
Escribí una oración temática y dos detalles
I used a word like also, first, or another
Usé una palabra como also, first o another

write.model: Our school custodian is a helpful member of our team. She cleans the classrooms and hallways every day. She also fixes broken chairs and doors.

familyTalk.en: On a walk, name a helper you see. Say a big idea about the helper and add two details.
familyTalk.es: Durante un paseo, nombren a un ayudante que vean. Digan una idea principal sobre esa persona y agreguen dos detalles.

teacherTip.en: Have pairs cross out the detail that does not belong and say why in a full sentence.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas tachen el detalle que no pertenece y expliquen por qué en una oración completa.

learn.rule: Start with a topic sentence. Then add details that all match the big idea, and leave out the ones that do not.
learn.ruleEs: Empieza con una oración temática. Luego agrega detalles que coincidan con la idea principal y deja fuera los que no.
learn.model: Squares are special shapes. All four sides are the same length. All four corners are square corners.
learn.notice: The topic sentence names the shape. Both details describe squares and nothing else.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence fits the three details about coins?
items.text: A penny is worth one cent. A nickel is worth five cents. A dime is worth ten cents.

options.text: A penny is worth one cent.
Coins are kept in a piggy bank.
Different coins are worth different amounts.

items.why: The topic sentence covers every detail. The first choice is just one detail, and the piggy bank is not in the details.
items.whyEs: La oración temática cubre todos los detalles. La primera opción es solo un detalle y la alcancía no aparece en los detalles.

items.prompt: Which sentence does not belong in the paragraph about number lines?
items.text: A number line helps us add and subtract. Numbers go in order from left to right. My grandmother grows red tomatoes. We hop forward to add.

options.text: My grandmother grows red tomatoes.
We hop forward to add.
Numbers go in order from left to right.

items.why: Details must be about the topic. Tomatoes have nothing to do with number lines, so that sentence should be removed.
items.whyEs: Los detalles deben tratar del tema. Los tomates no tienen nada que ver con las rectas numéricas, así que se quita esa oración.

items.prompt: Check every detail that belongs with this topic sentence: 'A triangle is a shape with three sides.'

options.text: A triangle also has three corners.
A circle is round and has no corners.
Some roofs have a triangle shape.
My brother has a blue backpack.

items.why: The details that belong are about triangles. The circle sentence is about a different shape.
items.whyEs: Los detalles correctos tratan de los triángulos. La oración del círculo trata de otra figura.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that adds one more detail about triangles.
items.model: A triangle has three sides. Also, it has three corners.
items.why: Also adds another detail on the same topic. The other words do not make sense in this sentence.
items.whyEs: Also agrega otro detalle sobre el mismo tema. Las otras palabras no tienen sentido en esta oración.

items.prompt: Put the sentences about adding on a number line in order.
lines: Adding two numbers is easy with a number line.
First, find the first number on the line.
Next, hop forward the second number of spaces.
Last, read the number where you land.
items.why: The big idea comes first. Then first, next, and last tell the steps in the order you do them.
items.whyEs: La idea principal va primero. Luego first, next y last dicen los pasos en el orden en que se hacen.

items.prompt: Which closing sentence best finishes the paragraph about triangles?
items.text: A triangle is a shape with three sides. It also has three corners. Many roofs are shaped like triangles.

options.text: A square has four sides.
So, a triangle is a shape with three sides and three corners.
I drew a triangle on Monday.

items.why: A closing sentence sums up the big idea in new words. The other choices change the topic or tell something small.
items.whyEs: Una oración final resume la idea principal con otras palabras. Las otras opciones cambian el tema o dicen algo pequeño.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two details about rectangles.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos detalles sobre los rectángulos.

label: I wrote a topic sentence and two details
Escribí una oración temática y dos detalles

write.model: Rectangles are useful shapes in our world. A door is a rectangle that lets us walk into a room. A book cover is also a rectangle.

familyTalk.en: Look around your home for one shape. Say a big idea about it and add two details.
familyTalk.es: Busquen en casa una figura. Digan una idea principal sobre ella y agreguen dos detalles.

teacherTip.en: Have students underline the topic sentence in green and each detail in blue before they write.
teacherTip.es: Pide que subrayen la oración temática en verde y cada detalle en azul antes de escribir.
